brief:
Middle East Eye reported that supporters of Israel are misrepresenting findings from a Unicef study measuring malnutrition levels in Gaza. The research showed lower rates of malnutrition across the enclave, a result that commentators said warrants acknowledgment. However, the outlet cautioned that improved malnutrition figures do not absolve responsibility for prior humanitarian conduct in the territory.

According to the report, advocates have selectively cited the Unicef data to counter broader claims about conditions facing Palestinians in Gaza. The malnutrition measurements, while distinct and quantifiable, represent only one dimension of the humanitarian situation. Critics argued that isolated statistics cannot erase documented suffering or questions of accountability for actions preceding the study period.

title: Israel backers distort Unicef data on Gaza malnutrition
